items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: have Pete Rugolo, Lennie Niehaus, Shorty Rogers, Marty Paich, you know Hank Levy — all the writers — Bill Russo, Bill Holman — everybody was still alive

ctx.x: important. But as you know, that’s not always the case. And a lot of times — and I think the idea behind the whole thing started back in the KLON days when I started to put — not only was I doing the events but also the radio shows that I’ve always done have been more like kind of documentary oriented. And it seems like doing it on a weekly basis that that would be, you know that I’ve, you know, always put a lot of effort into it, a lot of research and I’m kind of built that way in that I always kind of have to…

because people would get very excited over coming to see an alumni band playing. You know it all started with this big Stan Kenton event. I didn’t even intend for that — I never intended for that to be the case. But when I first moved to Los Angeles to take the job at the radio station I got one of the union directories that published Local 47 union directories and I started going through it just to see who was around, and I couldn’t believe that so many of — they still lived in the area, and the one thread that…
And it’s not going to be on YouTube just yet, right?
